summary: Customer payment failures are real and are caused by an expired mTLS client certificate in payment-service. The client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal reached notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; from ~12:10Z onward every call to bank-partner-api fails with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'. This drove bank_api_error_rate from 0.2% to 100% and payment_success_rate from ~99% to ~2.5%, while ~313 ERROR log lines and 140 PENDING_RETRY markings appear. The HTTP 5xx error_rate panel stayed green (~0.2%) because failed bank calls are recorded as PENDING_RETRY rather than 5xx, so the dashboard does not reflect the outage. All resource metrics (CPU, db pool, restarts), request rate, and other services (settlement, api-gateway) are normal, ruling out capacity/resource/deployment causes. Root-cause category: credential_expiry, originating in payment-service's own credential. Fix: renew/rotate the client cert and add expiry alerting.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service mTLS client certificate expired
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) used by payment-service to call bank-partner-api expired at 12:15:00Z. All outbound bank calls now fail TLS handshake (alert 45 certificate expired) and payments get marked PENDING_RETRY instead of completing, so real customers see failures while the HTTP 5xx error_rate panel stays green because the app returns a non-5xx outcome.

causal_chain.claim: Client cert notAfter=12:15:00Z reached, cert now invalid
Payments marked PENDING_RETRY instead of 5xx, so error_rate dashboard stays ~0.2%

assumptions: The expired cert is our own credential (payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) that we own and can rotate, not a vendor-managed cert
PENDING_RETRY payments do not eventually succeed automatically, matching customer complaints

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner API outage / dependency failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api (external) is degrading or rejecting traffic, causing payment failures. This is what the report's 'bank side' guess suggests.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The error is a TLS alert 45 specifically naming OUR client certificate's notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z expiry, not a partner-side 5xx/outage. Onset aligns exactly with the cert's expiry second, and the cert is our own CN, so the fault is our credential expiring rather than the partner degrading.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Raising the bank API timeout to 5000ms caused bank call failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The change was at 11:20Z, ~55 minutes before onset (~12:10Z), and the error is a TLS expired-certificate alert, unrelated to timeout duration. Raising a timeout would slow failures, not cause 'tls: expired certificate'.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deployment (settlement v1.9.0)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The only deployment was to settlement-service at 10:30Z, not payment-service; settlement-service logged zero errors; the failure is a TLS credential expiry which a CSV exporter change could not produce.

facts.statement: payment_success_rate fell from ~99% to ~2.5% beginning in the 12:10Z bucket and remained there.
bank_api_error_rate rose from 0.2% to 50% at 12:10Z and reached 100% from 12:20Z onward.

payment-service logs contain 171 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' entries naming CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, plus 140 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' PENDING_RETRY entries.
The only config change in the window was payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20Z (before onset).
The only deployment was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30Z, unrelated to payment-service.
payment-service CPU (~30%), db_pool_in_use (~8), and restarts (0) were all normal throughout.
request_rate was steady ~100 req/s, ruling out a traffic spike.
settlement-service and api-gateway logged zero errors, isolating the failure to payment-service's bank call path.

recommended_actions.action: Rotate/renew the mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and reload it into payment-service; verify bank-partner-api handshakes succeed.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cert's notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z has passed; all bank calls fail with alert 45 until a valid cert is presented.

recommended_actions.action: Reprocess the ~140+ payments marked PENDING_RETRY once the cert is valid so customers' transfers complete.
recommended_actions.rationale: Payments are stuck in PENDING_RETRY from the failed mTLS handshakes; customer impact persists until retried.

recommended_actions.action: Add an alert on client-certificate expiry (e.g. warn 14-30 days out) and on bank_api_error_rate / payment_success_rate, which would have caught this despite the green 5xx panel.
recommended_actions.rationale: The error_rate dashboard missed the incident; HIST-106 was the same failure mode and its resolution included an expiry alert.

recommended_actions.action: Automate certificate renewal/rotation to remove manual expiry risk.
recommended_actions.rationale: Repeat failure mode (HIST-106) attributed to 'no renewal automation'.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument bank-call outcomes as distinct signals (PENDING_RETRY, tls errors) so non-5xx failures surface on dashboards.
recommended_actions.rationale: Failed bank calls were recorded as PENDING_RETRY, not 5xx, hiding the outage from the error-rate panel.
